blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY – The city government of Iligan is bracing for the impacts of the projected “super” El Niño on the area’s agriculture and electricity supply. City officials discussed measures against El Niño’s impact during the 3rd Quarter Meeting of the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (CDRRMC) last Monday. Engr. Cristobal Tanael, of the City Agriculturist’s Office (CAO), said the effects of El Niño are already being felt through crop damage and reduced farm income in parts of the city.
